blind_target.title: The role of pronouns in young children’s acquisition of the English transitive construction.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The present study differs from Childers and Tomasello (2001) because only proforms such as he were provided in the noun phrases during the training session.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Hypothesis 2 was also disproved. The results showed that input consistency played a negative role for adult L2 construction learning.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: This paper explicitly retests the input-consistency benefit; the reported effect does not agree.

blind_target.authors: Goldberg, Adele E., Casenhiser, Devin & White, Tiffani.
blind_target.title: Constructions as categories of language: The role of order on construction learning.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Goldberg et al. (2007) showed that initially providing skewed input facilitated rapid construction generalization. The present study investigates this effect for the position of verbs with relative high token frequency.
blind_target.outcome_quote: There was a significant main effect for order of frequent verbs in the comprehension of the APPEARANCE construction. Figure 1 shows that the (+forward order) group outperformed the (−forward skewing) group. No significant effects were found in the guided production of the APPEARANCE construction and the comprehension of the Samoan ergative construction.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors present an agreeing comprehension effect and explicitly absent effects in the other tasks; no overall verdict supersedes this comparison.

luna_triage.reason: The full text tests whether Childers and Tomasello's reported input-consistency effect generalizes to adult L2 construction learning. It explicitly describes the consistency manipulation, asks whether the effect occurs, and reports negative consistency effects on comprehension. The supplied Casenhiser and Goldberg row is a different original paper.
